P1.evidence: No setter code in the title and no setter referenced, so the read-back check does not apply. As a second call the rep did bridge properly — 'obviously you and I spoke yesterday. Just kind of picking up from where we left off' — and set two of the four frame elements, goals and blockers: 'we all have our goals, whatever they may be, but there's always, always things, there's blockers that are preventing us in the past from actually reaching that.' No 'where you are' baseline element, no 'what you need' element, and no agreement question. The opening question was a root-cause question rather than the scripted open: 'what do you think has kind of prevented you from being there thus far?'

P2.evidence: CAVEAT: this is a second call and the prior conversation is not in this batch, so Baseline may have been run on 05/02. On what is observable here, only age and diet were covered. Age was asked twice — 'Remind me, how old are you, Omar?' then 'And how old are you, Omar?' — and answered 36; height and weight were never obtained. Diet was properly probed: 'is your nutrition protocol dialed in as it stands right now? Or is it kind of inconsistent?' followed by the work-meals discovery and 'are you opposed to doing a meal prep for yourself once a week?'. Nothing else. The rep never asked what Omar does for a living — the youth-work reference was volunteered inside an unrelated answer — and never asked about health conditions, injuries, movement limitations, his current training week, results, sleep or energy. He then sold a loaded kettlebell programme and referred the entire physical assessment forward: 'before we design either of these programs for you, we need to understand what the hell is baseline for Omar.'

P3.evidence: An unusual shape: the deep half of Phase 3 ran beautifully and the surface half did not run at all. The bridge was made explicitly — 'can you see this is not just about swinging a kettlebell around? It's not a kettlebell. The kettlebell is just a vehicle, brother' — and the impact question landed the richest answer of the call: 'I'd be able to get stronger and gain strength for my coworkers and for the youth that I work with... I'd be able to take my dog on more walks.' The who-else move and the drive-through to identity both ran, reaching faith and purpose: 'Most important in my life now is my relationship with my higher power', 'I know that I'm called for a higher purpose.' What never happened is the physical half. No 'what one thing would you change', no mobility-strength-energy question, no 'what's something physical you want to do but can't'. The rep sold a body-composition programme without ever asking the prospect what he wants his body to do or look like.

P4.evidence: Root cause was excellent, past attempts were skipped entirely. 'What has kept you stuck in the past will find a way to keep you stuck in the future' opened it, and the follow-through was patient — 'is this something that you've always known, or is it something that you've just come to awareness when we've spoken?' and 'You're not continuing to try when things get hard. What would you say that's kind of cost you so far?'. The prospect named his own gap unprompted and precisely: 'being used to failing... I don't continue to try. If it's too hard, I just get used to it' and later 'I'm comfortable with average.' But the rep never asked what he has tried before or what happened with it, which is why no prior programme, trainer, gym or diet is on record anywhere in this file. The information-isn't-the-problem move was implied rather than delivered — the prospect got there himself with 'I have the knowledge of what I'm supposed to eat. Unfortunately, I eat whatever is there for me.'

P5.evidence: The best-run Consequence Frame in this batch and worth using as a training clip. The two-route future was drawn cleanly: 'you honestly have two routes in front of you right now, Omar. You can continue just being patient with yourself and letting time continue, waiting for something big or not so big to happen which pushes you over the edge. Or you can use this sense of awareness to actually make a change.' The settle-for question was asked without softening: 'Are you willing to change the fuel from a want to a need? Or are you cool just maintaining yourself as you are and having all these areas in your life not be up to standard?' The why-not was pursued twice, including 'I'm curious as to why this isn't, I guess, a need for yourself' and 'What shifted recently has put you in a state of desperation for it to be a need?' The line in the sand produced the strongest commitment of the call: 'Choosing. Choosing to do it, whether I feel it or not. That's the route that will lead me to my best self.'

P6.evidence: The trust gauge ran but after the pillars rather than before, and it returned an 8 with an explicitly self-directed reason: 'Why am I not here at the 12?' — 'Because I know people, and I know myself.' That is precisely the hesitation the script says to route back to Phase 5 on, and instead the rep asked what gave him confidence and then moved to price. The all-in question was never asked. Had it been, the two blockers that consumed the following forty minutes — a $600/mo ceiling and a need to review options in writing — would have surfaced before the offer rather than after it. The rep did make a second attempt at a commitment check at 01:02:26 with the mirror-at-37 question, but by then the pillars were already delivered.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted repeatedly across roughly forty minutes and refused each time, including the fallback $100 deposit. No payment was taken, so the Trevor booking, the agreement email and the welcome-email sequence were all unreachable. Scoring them as misses would penalise the rep for a phase the call could not arrive at.

objection_plays.detail: Roughly half the play ran, and the half that was skipped is the half that matters most. Ran: the break-it-up offer ('Most people, man, they just put it on a credit card, but we have different in-house payment plan options if necessary'), the permission question ('I just got to understand things from a high level to see what we can do. You open to me asking you a couple of questions?'), cash on hand, monthly surplus ($500-700), and credit score (above 720). Not run: the ISOLATE FIRST move, which the script puts before everything else — the rep never asked whether anything other than money was in the way, so when the real second blocker turned out to be his decision process, it arrived unhandled forty minutes later. Also not run: number of credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, and crypto/stocks/investments. The 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' frame was never used.

Triggered three times and played through at length, arguably well past its useful life. Ran: the direct probe ('the only question that you need to ask yourself in this moment, why am I not moving forward right now?'), the callback to his own words ('from earlier in our conversation, you said to me specifically, because I noted it down, that you know within yourself that you can't continue like this'), the deposit fallback borrowed from Objection B, and a heavy version of the deciding-not-thinking frame ('Whenever anyone says they need to think about it... it's really, really low probability that we ever hit back from them'). Not run: 'Do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal?' and 'That man you want to be — how does HE decide right now?', which are the two moves that would have worked on a prospect this identity-driven. The play was run to completion and then continued past the point where the prospect had disengaged.

Two distinct doubts surfaced and neither got the play. The self-doubt behind the 8/10 — 'Because I know people, and I know myself' — is a fear-of-failure statement from a man who has just described a lifelong pattern of quitting, and the rep answered it with 'What gives you the confidence to say an 8?' rather than any part of Objection E. The BURNED BEFORE move was sitting right there and was never used. The second doubt was about the service: 'I have my doubts on 60 people. That's wild.' Neither the certainty question, the bridge, nor the plane analogy was attempted.

SCRIPT GAP — service capacity. The prospect ran a genuine due-diligence line on delivery: 'that's 60 people that have Trevor's number and are reaching out to him at any point in the day' and 'even if half of that were to reach out to him on a daily basis, that's quite a bit.' The playbook has no answer for a prospect who does the arithmetic on a single-coach model. The rep improvised a touchpoint-decay explanation and conceded the scaling problem outright — 'When the business inevitably grows and scales, we have thousands of, you know, we have to figure out alternative strategies' — which is honest and unhelpful. This will recur with any analytical buyer.

SCRIPT GAP — the deliberate decision-maker. The prospect's blocker was neither money nor belief but process, and he articulated it clearly and repeatedly: 'if I lay all my options out, and think through each option clearly, not on a call, not on video, that, to me, seems more like who I am.' The playbook has exactly one interpretation of any request for time, which is avoidance, so the rep treated a stated decision style as a character flaw and escalated. He also volunteered the root cause as feedback the company should have: 'because so many options were laid out, now I have to kind of go through each option and see which would benefit me the most in the long run.' There is no scripted path for sending a written option summary and closing on a booked follow-up, which is what this call needed.

SCRIPT GAP — the principled non-borrower. 'I'm not the type of person to put stuff on credit card. That's just not who I am as a person' is a values statement, not a capacity statement, and Objection C has no branch for it. The financial-picture questions in the script are built around credit cards and available credit, so a prospect who rules out credit on principle takes the play offline entirely. What followed — routing him into Klarna — is the predictable outcome of a script with no alternative path.

notes: Phases 3 and 5 are the best work in this folder and should be clipped for training — the route A / route B frame and the want-versus-need sequence produced real commitment from a genuinely stuck prospect. The call was then lost in the offer, not in the discovery. Four tiers plus three financing schedules across two lenders were put in front of a self-described analyser, and he told the rep in as many words that the option count was what stopped him. Two concrete coaching points: isolate before opening the wallet, so the second blocker surfaces before the first is solved; and when a prospect states a decision style rather than an objection, the correct move is a written summary and a firm booked follow-up, not escalation. The last twenty minutes did damage that a better-structured close would not have needed to risk.
